meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The exam was a piece of cake after all the practice.
origin: The origin is uncertain; one idea is that a slice of cake is an easy and pleasant thing to eat

wrong_meanings.meaning: a dessert served at a party
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one
The idiom is about difficulty, not about hunger or wanting food
The idiom refers to ease of doing something, not to the cost of a thing

explanation: 'A piece of cake' describes a task that is very easy to complete. It is used in everyday speech to say that something did not require much effort.
